reading.body:
A founding OpenAI CTO launched Thinking Machines Lab in February 2025 to build collaborative, multimodal AI systems that work with people rather than pursuing full autonomy.

Murati's departure from OpenAI after nearly six years, including a stint as interim CEO during the November 2023 board crisis, marked a shift in focus within the AI leadership class. Her new company's stated philosophy centers on human-AI collaboration rather than systems designed for independent operation. This represents a distinct position in the market at a time when debate over AI autonomy remains unresolved.

The company's emphasis on multimodal systems and collaboration means Thinking Machines Lab operates in a narrower technical scope than the large-scale model training that dominates compute infrastructure discussion. The data provided does not specify the company's compute requirements, funding, facilities, or power consumption, making it impossible to assess how its technical approach translates to infrastructure demands. What the company prioritizes and how those priorities affect resource intensity remain separate questions.

standing.watch: What remains unresolved in the records is the fate of the OpenAI cases, all of which are filed with docket monitoring active and no development recorded yet by this tracker. The dates attached to several of them, including Bass v. OpenAI, LLC, United States v. OpenAI OpCo LLC, JIANG v. OPENAI GROUP PBC, Smigelski v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC, GRANT v. OPENAI INC, and Vredenburgh v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC, fall in September 2026, while TradeSun, Inc. v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC carries no date in the record. Buist v. Anthropic, PBC is likewise filed with no development recorded. The records do not show any pending case, planned listing or dispute directly involving Thinking Machines Lab, so what comes next for Murati's own company is not yet documented here.
standing.record: The site's records place Murati at the center of two companies, OpenAI and Thinking Machines Lab, and connect her OpenAI tenure to a series of lawsuits naming OpenAI entities. Those cases include TradeSun, Inc. v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC, Bass v. OpenAI, LLC, United States v. OpenAI OpCo LLC, JIANG v. OPENAI GROUP PBC, Smigelski v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC, GRANT v. OPENAI INC, and Vredenburgh v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC, all filed with docket monitoring active and no development recorded yet by this tracker. One further case, Buist v. Anthropic, PBC, names a different company and does not involve OpenAI. The pattern running through the record is a cluster of unresolved filings against OpenAI entities alongside Murati's move from OpenAI leadership to founding her own lab.
standing.standing: Mira Murati stands as the founder and CEO of Thinking Machines Lab, a public benefit corporation she founded in 2025 and launched publicly on February 18, 2025, focused on collaborative, multimodal AI systems. She is also recorded as an executive of OpenAI, the San Francisco startup founded in 2015, where she became Chief Technology Officer in May 2022 and briefly served as interim CEO starting November 17, 2023, during the board crisis following Sam Altman's departure. She announced her departure from OpenAI on September 25, 2024, after nearly six years there. The records show her influence running through both companies, with her current control centered on Thinking Machines Lab as its chief executive.
